title: Stance & Motion
summary: The base of all folkstyle wrestling: good posture, feet shoulder-width, constant motion.
steps: Stagger feet, lead leg slightly forward
Knees bent, hips back, back straight
Hands out at shoulder height
Never cross feet, keep moving
keyPoints: Head up, eyes forward
Weight on balls of feet
Motion forces opponents to react
commonMistakes: Squatting too low with a straight back

title: Penetration Step
summary: The explosive first step that closes distance on every shot.
steps: Level change first, then step
Long step past the lead foot
Back knee drives to the mat
Chin through the side, chest up
keyPoints: Step with the lead leg past the opponent's foot
Get hips under shoulders
commonMistakes: Dropping the head before the step

title: Level Change
summary: Drop hips without telegraphing the shot.
steps: Bend knees, not the waist
Keep chest tall and head up
Change levels 2-3 times to test reaction
keyPoints: Hips down, not head down

title: Hand Fighting
summary: Win the wrist battle to open shots and shut down theirs.
steps: Control the inside wrist
Snap and circle to off-balance
Clear ties before you shoot
keyPoints: Inside tie wins most exchanges
commonMistakes: Passive hands, letting them control ties

title: Pummeling for Underhooks
summary: Slide your arms inside to win underhooks from collar-and-elbow.
steps: Fight inside position on both arms
Duck one arm under, then the other
Circle away from their overhook
keyPoints: Head on the same side as your underhook
commonMistakes: Pummeling flat instead of at an angle

title: Double-Leg Takedown
summary: The highest-percentage takedown in wrestling.
steps: Level change and penetration step
Head outside or inside on their hip
Clasp hands behind both knees
Drive diagonally, turn the corner
keyPoints: Head tight to their side, never centered
Run your feet, finish through the mat

title: High Crotch
summary: Single-leg variant that keeps your head up and finish options open.
steps: Penetration step to the side
Grab behind the knee, high on the thigh
Head up on their hip, pull the leg to your chest
Finish with a run or lift
keyPoints: Keep your head higher than their hip
commonMistakes: Head down, getting rolled over the top

title: Single-Leg Finish: Run the Pipe
summary: Classic finish once you have the leg: trap it and run the pipe.
steps: Lock the leg between yours
Trap the ankle with your outside foot
Run your chest down the leg
Head up, hand post if needed
keyPoints: Chin up, chest heavy on the thigh

title: Fireman's Carry
summary: Countering their pressure with a classic head-and-arm carry.
steps: Duck under their collar tie
Capture head and same-side arm
Drop to one knee, spin across
Land them on their back
keyPoints: Sell the level change before the spin
commonMistakes: Slow spin, letting them sprawl on top

title: Knee Tap
summary: Off-balance tap that needs no penetration step.
steps: Off-balance them with a snap or pull
Step through, tap the knee
Drive through with your chest
keyPoints: Off-balance first, tap second

title: Snap Down to Front Headlock
summary: Snap the head down and spin behind.
steps: Collar tie hard, snap down in a circle
Wrap the front headlock
Spin behind for the takedown
keyPoints: Snap and circle, not straight down

title: Fake Shot to Re-Attack
summary: Use a fake level change to open their defense.
steps: Show the penetration step
When they sprawl, circle behind
Finish with a front headlock or second shot
keyPoints: Make the fake look real

title: Chain Wrestling
summary: Never end on a lost move: flow from every failed attack to the next.
steps: Shot stuffed → front headlock or re-shot
Underhook denied → snap down
Always move on the reaction
keyPoints: Attack in pairs, not singles
commonMistakes: Resetting to neutral after every failed shot

title: Sprawl
summary: The first and most important defense to a shot.
steps: Snap hips back and down
Legs back, chest heavy on their shoulders
Whizzer or cross-face, then circle behind
keyPoints: Hips to the mat, not just legs back
commonMistakes: Kicking legs back while staying tall
Sprawling straight back without dropping hips

title: Front Headlock Series
summary: Control from a sprawl: near-wrist, headlock, spin behind.
steps: Lock the front headlock, chest heavy
Grab the near wrist to block the scramble
Spin behind or finish a guillotine-style trip
keyPoints: Kill the near wrist first
commonMistakes: Riding high on the shoulders, losing the wrist

title: Mat Return
summary: From a front headlock, drive them back to the mat.
steps: Front headlock with a whizzer
Drive at an angle across their base
Steer them to their hip and sit them down
keyPoints: Angle, not straight-ahead pushing

title: Stand-Up (Bottom)
summary: The safest escape from the referee's position.
steps: Get to your base, hand control
Drive up off the far leg
Clear the hips, turn and face
keyPoints: Straight up the ladder — vertical, not forward
Hand fight the moment you stand

title: Sit-Out Turn
summary: Turn away from pressure to escape or reverse.
steps: Feel the pressure direction
Sit through toward the open side
Turn the corner and face or spin behind
keyPoints: Sit INTO the pressure hole, not away

title: Hip Heist
summary: Explosive reverse that flips pressure into back points.
steps: Build a base as they ride legs
Switch hips under their weight
Heist the hips through and take the back
keyPoints: Timing: heist as their weight shifts

title: Roll to Escape
summary: When they're heavy on top, roll to create space.
steps: Trap a wrist or ankle as you roll
Roll across your far shoulder
Come up facing them, hand fight, stand
keyPoints: Grab something before you roll

title: Top Breakdown: Near Arm Far Leg
summary: The fundamental breakdown that flattens an opponent.
steps: Chest on their back, near arm trapped
Far leg captured with your foot
Spiral your weight through them
keyPoints: Kill the near arm before anything else

title: Leg Riding
summary: Ride legs to force movement and open turns.
steps: Spiral in, lock the far leg
Keep your hips heavy and low
Switch between legs to force reactions
keyPoints: Stay on your hip, never flat

title: Defending the Half Nelson
summary: Stop the most common turn before it starts.
steps: Hand fight the far side immediately
Keep your elbows in and hips low
Build your base and clear the arm
keyPoints: Deny the underhook early
commonMistakes: Letting them lock the half while you're flat

title: Tilt
summary: The workhorse turn: four points from one tilt series.
steps: Near arm trapped, far arm over the back
Roll them up onto their side
Hook the far arm, tilt, repeat
keyPoints: Lock the near wrist to your chest

title: Cradle
summary: The pinning combination that ends matches.
steps: Break them down to their side
Capture head and far knee
Lock hands, squeeze head to knee
Roll them onto their back
keyPoints: Their head and knee must touch
commonMistakes: Riding high so they can block the lock

title: Arm Bar Turn
summary: Classic wing turn from the referee's position.
steps: Trap the near arm against your chest
Wing the far arm over their back
Drive your chest through for the turn
keyPoints: First the near arm, then the wing
commonMistakes: Winging the arm before trapping the near one

title: Ankle Pick from Ride
summary: Turn the ankle to open the far side.
steps: Control the near ankle between your legs
Turn the ankle inward
Reach across for the far arm or tilt
keyPoints: Ankle control kills their base
commonMistakes: Loose ankle grip letting them kick free

title: Pinning Combinations
summary: Flow from turn to turn until the pin.
steps: Start with a tilt or arm bar
As they defend, switch to the counter-turn
Chain: tilt → cradle → arm bar → pin
keyPoints: Every turn has a built-in counter-turn

title: Re-Attacking the Sprawler
summary: Their sprawl is your setup.
steps: Get sprawled on: front headlock or whizzer
Circle to the open side
Re-shot at the angle they gave you
keyPoints: Sprawlers give their legs back — take them

title: Off-Balancing Drills
summary: Wins matches before any shot: snaps, shucks, pulls.
steps: Snap, pull, and circle in sets of 5
Watch their base break
Attack the direction they stumble
keyPoints: Off-balance first, shot second

title: Closing Distance Safely
summary: Get to your offense without eating a shot.
steps: Move at angles, not straight lines
Clear their hands with a slap and circle
Enter on your terms, level change first
keyPoints: Never close straight into their offense
commonMistakes: Walking straight in with hands low

title: Footwork & Angles
summary: Circle to create angles, attack from the side.
steps: Constant half-circle motion
Step into their lead side
Attack when their feet cross
keyPoints: Attack when they cross their feet

title: Posture in the Clinch
summary: Stay strong when they tie up with you.
steps: Hips back, spine tall
Fight the inside position
Break their posture with a collar tie
keyPoints: Whoever controls posture controls the exchange

title: Match Conditioning Circuit
summary: Wrestling-specific gas tank: 6 rounds of 90 seconds.
steps: Sprawl x10
Stand-up x10
Sprawl to re-shot x10
Rest 30s, repeat 6 rounds
keyPoints: Train the positions you wrestle in

title: Hand Speed & Reaction
summary: Faster hands win the first tie every time.
steps: Partner slaps, you block in 30s sets
Wrist-control sparring
Reaction sprawl drills
keyPoints: Eyes on the chest, react to the shoulders
commonMistakes: Watching the hands instead of the body

title: Whizzer Series
summary: Kill their underhook and create offense.
steps: Overhook the underhooking arm
Drop your weight, spike the whizzer
Circle behind or mat return
keyPoints: The whizzer is a weapon, not just defense

title: Headlock Defense
summary: Don't get thrown: kill the lock early.
steps: Feel the arm wrap — post the near leg immediately
Grab their locking hands and peel
Turn in toward the lock, never away
keyPoints: Turn INTO the headlock

title: Duck Under
summary: From collar tie, duck to the back for an easy takedown.
steps: Collar tie hard, pull down
Duck the same-side arm under theirs
Come up behind, waist lock, take them down
keyPoints: Pull their head down as you duck

title: Ankle Pick
summary: Slick counter from an open tie.
steps: Open their elbows with a pull
Cross-step and catch the ankle
Drive through with the shoulder
keyPoints: Off-balance up, pick down

title: Switch (Bottom)
summary: Turn defense into a reversal from the base.
steps: Feel the far-side pressure
Switch hips, block their near leg
Face them and score the reversal
keyPoints: The switch blocks their leg as you turn

title: Peterson Roll
summary: Sneaky reversal from a flat ride.
steps: When they cross-face, roll to your chest
Grab their ankle and roll through
Come up on top for the reversal
keyPoints: Commit fully — hesitation kills the roll
commonMistakes: Half-rolling and stopping on the side

title: Ride with Pressure Changes
summary: Alternate heavy and light pressure to force mistakes.
steps: Heavy chest, then float
When they react, attack the open side
Switch rides: legs, spiral, ankle
keyPoints: Reactions create turns

title: Scramble Bail-Outs
summary: When a scramble goes bad, get back to neutral safely.
steps: Keep a hand on a leg or wrist always
Head up, never face-down under them
Sit to your hip, frame and reset
keyPoints: In scrambles, control beats speed
commonMistakes: Turning your back in a scramble

title: Double-Underhooks Body Lock
summary: Heavy upper-body takedown from double unders.
steps: Pummel to double underhooks
Lock hands, chest tight
Lift or step behind and trip
keyPoints: Get your hips under theirs before lifting
commonMistakes: Locking low and getting choked out of position
